title: Crop Residue Management

short_description: Crop residue management involves leaving stover and other trash from cereal crops (including tef, wheat and maize), as well as haulms of legumes, in the field. Crop residues keep the soil covered, retain organic matter and moisture in the soil, and help to ensure better production.

activities.description: Mowing the crop by leaving some proportion on the ground.
Plow over the crop residue early on.
Keep the farm with crop residue intact from livestock

costs.comments: Costs were calculated per Technology area. The technology needs changing the mindset of the land users more than money for establishment and maintenance.

adoption.comments: Land users adopted the practice and plow over the crop residue when the first shower of rainfall intercepted.

strengths: It improves soil fertility on gradual basis.
It assists to reduce soil acidity.
Absorbs and retains soil moisture for the crop to rely on for growth and grain filling as a coping mechanism to the unpredictable distribution of rainfall.
It reduces soil temperature and smothers the weeds.
Sequesters carbon, beneficial for climate change/variability.
weaknesses: Creates tillage inconvenience as mechanization is less common among smallholders. Overcome by using the excessive residue as trash line to support soil and water conservation.
Free grazing system and multiple uses of crop residue challenge retention of crop residue. Overcome by institutionalizing a controlled grazing system.
Less fodder available for livestock and other multiple uses of crop residues. Overcome by limiting retained residue to 15-30 percent of total non-grain biomass.
